_provenance.author: study authors
_provenance.not_derived_from: training rows, test rows, or any inspection of how annotators actually applied these labels
_provenance.why_this_matters: HANDOVER §4 claims fine-tuning transfers the annotation convention rather than the task. If these glosses encoded the convention -- learned by reading labelled examples -- the `glosses` rung would smuggle that supervision into the prompt and the claim could not be tested cleanly. They are therefore written from the label names alone, which is exactly the information a practitioner has when they write a prompt for their own taxonomy. Where two labels are near-synonymous from their names (the card and top-up pairs), the glosses are correspondingly near-identical. That is not a defect in the glosses; it is the finding.
_provenance.suggested_followup: A second, deliberately convention-disclosing gloss file is the sharpest direct test of §4: if prose that states the annotation rule for the five contested intents closes the five-class gap, the thesis is demonstrated without relying on the encoder at all. Keep it as a separate file and a separate rung -- do not edit this one.
